components.css: .ds-stepper ol { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; } .ds-stepper li { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; } .ds-step { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; padding: 6px 12px; border-radius: 9999px; font: 500 0.875rem/1.25 Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; color: var(--color-df-muted, #6b7280); text-decoration: none; transition: background-color 150ms ease-out; } .ds-step:hover { background: #f3f4f6; } .ds-step:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-df-primary, #7c3aed); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-step-badge { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 20px; height: 20px; border-radius: 9999px; font: 700 11px/1 Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; background: #f3f4f6; color: var(--color-df-muted, #6b7280); } .ds-step-done { color: var(--color-df-ink, #111827); } .ds-step-done .ds-step-badge { background: var(--color-df-primary, #7c3aed); color: #fff; } .ds-step-current { background: var(--color-df-primary, #7c3aed); color: #fff; } .ds-step-current:hover { background: var(--color-df-primary, #7c3aed); } .ds-step-current .ds-step-badge { background: rgb(255 255 255 / 0.2); color: #fff; } .ds-step-line { width: 24px; height: 1px; background: #d1d5db; }

narrative.overview:
Vision Craft is a clean, well-lit workspace. Like a photographer's studio with white walls and good light, the interface stays calm so the photos can be loud. The chrome is near-white in light mode (deep midnight navy in dark mode), the text is graphite, and one violet tells you where to act. Everything colorful on screen should be the user's own images.

The personality is soft and confident: generous pill-shaped controls, semibold labels, rounded cards with hairline borders, and big heavy headings that settle each page in two lines. Density is relaxed. This is a four-step wizard for someone who isn't a designer, so each screen carries one main idea, one primary action, and plenty of air. Surfaces rest flat; lift and shadow appear only as feedback.

Two themes are first-class. Every color token has a night twin, and the theme is a class on `<html>` (`.dark`, persisted as `df-theme`). The night theme is midnight navy with slate surfaces, not inverted gray.
keyCharacteristics: Neutral, bright chrome; the photos supply the color.
One violet (#7c3aed / #a78bfa at night) for action, selection, and current state.
A violet-to-teal gradient used only on the single main forward button on a screen.
Inter throughout, in heavy display weights over quiet small labels.
Pills for controls, soft 16–24px rectangles for containers.
Flat at rest; lift and violet-tinted shadow only on hover, selection, or floating layers.

rules.name: The Photos Carry the Color Rule
rules.body: The chrome stays neutral. Violet is the only interface hue a user should notice; if a screen looks colorful before any images load, something is over-decorated.

rules.name: The One Gradient Rule
rules.body: The violet-to-teal gradient (`linear-gradient(to right, violet, lagoon)`) is reserved for the single main forward action on a screen: "Crear mi primer board", "Armar Board", the advance-to-export button, the print confirm. One per screen. Every other primary button is solid violet.

rules.name: The Night Twin Rule
rules.body: Every `df-*` color is written with its `-dark` twin (`bg-df-surface dark:bg-df-surface-dark`). A light token used alone is a bug in night mode.

rules.name: The Violet Second Line Rule
rules.body: A wizard step's page heading is two lines: a plain Graphite line, then a violet line that ends with a period ("Diseña tu / **Visión.**"). The eyebrow above it names the step. Don't add a third line or move the violet to the first line.

rules.name: The Whisper Label Rule
rules.body: Section labels are tiny, bold, uppercase, widely tracked, and muted. They organize, they don't compete. Headings shout; labels whisper; nothing sits loudly in between.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: At rest, a surface gets a hairline border and nothing heavier than Rest. Lift appears as a response to hover or selection; Float only for things that genuinely sit above the page. A card with `shadow-lg` at rest is wrong.

rules.name: The Violet Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows that signal selection or action are tinted violet (10–30%). Neutral black shadows are only for floating layers.

rules.name: The Pill Means Press Rule
rules.body: If it's fully rounded, it's interactive or it's a status mark. Containers never become pills, and primary buttons never drop to square-ish corners.

dos: **Do** keep the chrome neutral (Studio Mist / Paper White / Graphite / Pewter) and let violet mark only action, selection, and current state.
**Do** write every `df-*` color with its `-dark` twin, and check both themes.
**Do** use pills for anything pressable and 16px / 24px rounded rectangles for anything that contains.
**Do** keep surfaces flat at rest (hairline + Rest shadow at most); add Lift (−2px, violet-tinted shadow) only on hover or selection.
**Do** set step headings as two lines with the violet, period-ended second line, under a 10px tracked uppercase eyebrow.
**Do** use a 2px violet ring or border for selected states, plus a violet check badge when the item is a photo.
**Do** give every interactive element a visible focus state: 2px violet outline, 2px offset.
**Do** use `df-*` tokens for new UI; when a needed token doesn't exist (border, alt surface), add it to `@theme` in `src/assets/app.css` rather than reaching for raw Tailwind grays or hex.
donts: **Don't** use the violet-to-teal gradient on more than one button per screen, or on anything that isn't the main forward action.
**Don't** use Marigold until it has a defined role.
**Don't** use DaisyUI stock component classes (`btn-outline`, `select-bordered`, `alert-success`, `bg-base-*`) for new UI; they're off-system drift.
**Don't** reference undefined tokens (`df-border`, `df-surface-alt`, `animate-fade-in`, `animate-fade-in-up`); they silently render nothing.
**Don't** put heavy shadows (`shadow-lg` and up) on resting cards; those belong to Lift, Glow, and Float.
**Don't** make containers pill-shaped or give primary buttons small square-ish corners.
**Don't** add decorative color to the chrome (tinted section backgrounds, colored icons, multicolor badges); the photos are the color.
